title: Integral closure commutes with finite products
statement: Let $R_i\to S_i$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings for $i=1,\dots,n$, let $R=\prod_iR_i$ and $S=\prod_iS_i$, and let $S_i'\subseteq S_i$ be the subring of elements integral over $R_i$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then the subring of $S$ consisting of elements integral over $R$ is exactly $\prod_iS_i'$. If every $R_i\to S_i$ is injective, so that $R\subseteq S$, then $R$ is integrally closed in $S$ if and only if each $R_i$ is integrally closed in $S_i$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0CY9 (lemma-finite-product-integral-closure, line 7583), using Tag 0CY8 for coordinatewise integrality

proof.text: Let $s=(s_i)\in S$ be integral over $R$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], a monic polynomial $P(T)\in R[T]$ satisfies $P(s)=0$. Projecting each coefficient of $P$ to $R_i$ produces a monic polynomial $P_i(T)\in R_i[T]$. Projection of the equality $P(s)=0$ gives $P_i(s_i)=0$, so every $s_i$ is integral over $R_i$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0CY8 (lemma-finite-product-integral, forward implication; proof omitted)

proof.text: Conversely, suppose every $s_i$ is integral over $R_i$. For each $i$, choose a monic $P_i(T)\in R_i[T]$ with $P_i(s_i)=0$ and degree $d_i$. Choose a common integer $D\ge1$ with $D\ge d_i$ for all $i$, and put $Q_i(T)=T^{D-d_i}P_i(T)$. Then $Q_i$ is monic of degree $D$ and $Q_i(s_i)=0$. At each degree $0,\dots,D$, assemble the coefficients of the $Q_i$ into an element of $R=\prod_iR_i$; the resulting $Q(T)\in R[T]$ is monic and has $Q(s)=0$ coordinatewise. Hence $s$ is integral over $R$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For an empty product, $R$ and $S$ are zero rings and the same conclusion holds with $Q(T)=T$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0CY8 (lemma-finite-product-integral, reverse implication; proof omitted)

proof.text: An element $s=(s_i)$ belongs to the integral closure of $R$ in $S$ exactly when every $s_i$ belongs to $S_i'$, by Steps 1 and 2 and [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Equality of these subsets, hence of the subrings, follows. If all component maps are injective, their product is injective and identifies $R$ with $\prod_iR_i\subseteq S$. Under this identification the equality of integral closures says $R=\prod_iS_i'$ exactly when $R_i=S_i'$ for every $i$, including the empty-product case.
